summary.oneLiner: Cohance reported a 13% FY26 revenue decline driven by destocking of two large commercial molecules and Nacharam site disruptions, marking a cyclical bottom with management guiding for H2FY27 recovery. The strategic pivot under new CEO Umang Vohra focuses on de-risking concentration via a diversified Phase 3 pipeline (10 programs) and scaling high-value ADC/oligonucleotide capabilities, though near-term margins face pressure from geopolitical logistics costs.

one-line thesis: Cohance reported a 13% FY26 revenue decline driven by destocking of two large commercial molecules and Nacharam site disruptions, marking a cyclical bottom with management guiding for H2FY27 recovery. The strategic pivot under new CEO Umang Vohra focuses on de-risking concentration via a diversified Phase 3 pipeline (10 programs) and scaling high-value ADC/oligonucleotide capabilities, though near-term margins face pressure from geopolitical logistics costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 22.68B (-13% YoY); Adj EBITDA INR 4.77B (21% margin, standalone 24.6%); PAT impacted by INR 321M one-offs (INR 195M inventory provision + INR 126M customer adjustments); Order book skewed to H2FY27; Net debt not explicitly quantified but free cash flow INR 1.73B generated.
guidance: Revenue/EBITDA: Q1FY27 weak (low point), Q2 stable, strong growth from H2FY27; Margins: Q1FY27 gross margin hit by 100-150 bps due to Middle East logistics/input inflation; Order inflow: Reload conversion >90%, 10 Phase 3 programs; Capex: INR 3B expected in FY27.
order book & pipeline: 140+ active CDMO projects; 10 Phase 3 programs (2 recently commercialized); 4 commercial orders received for one new molecule (revenue expected Q2/Q3 FY27); API+ order visibility improving post-Nacharam stabilization.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pharma CDMO: INR 8.89B FY26, underlying early single-digit growth ex-destocking, 70% from commercial products. API+: INR 10.88B (-8% YoY), impacted by INR 610M Nacharam disruption, now stabilizing. Specialty Chem: INR 2.91B (-2.1% YoY), FY27 is qualification year with growth expected in FY28.
growth verticals / optionality: ADC payload/linker expansion (3 DMFs filed); NJ Bio US facility expansion ($10M capex) for bioconjugation; Oligonucleotide cGMP facility validation; 10 Phase 3 pipeline converting to commercial over 12-18 months.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 Gross Margin 70.8%; Q1FY27 headwind of 100-150 bps from logistics/raw material inflation (Middle East); One-time expenses included INR 400Cr+ conversion costs and INR 260Cr marketing/brand building (post-merger).
capex / expansion: INR 2.15B spent in FY26 (ADC, oligo, quality systems); INR 3B planned for FY27; $10M specific expansion at NJ Bio US facility.
capital allocation: Focus on capacity expansion for ADC/oligo, quality system upgrades, and working capital normalization; No M&A or buyback mentioned; Priority on organic pipeline conversion.
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration (historical reliance on 2 large molecules); Geopolitical logistics cost inflation; Regulatory timing for new commercial launches; Delayed reloads from innovator partners.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges 'bottoming out' phase; Emphasizes operational rigor and governance under new CEO; Transparent on Q1 weakness but firm on H2 recovery narrative.
non-obvious takeaways: Niche tech (ADC/Oligo) contributed 16.2% of revenue; Top 15 API products contribute ~50% of API+ revenue but concentration is decreasing YoY; AI tools currently limited to internal analysis/regulatory filing efficiency, not core R&D acceleration yet.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Destocking of two large molecules created a revenue vacuum of ~INR 2.6B in FY26, pressuring sector peers with similar concentration risks. | Generic CDMO peers with high single-client dependency | loser | Med | Cohance's diversification into 10 Phase 3 programs may outperform peers stuck in single-molecule cycles. |
| Geopolitical tensions in Middle East escalating logistics/freight costs by 100-150 bps for Q1FY27. | Indian API exporters with high Middle East exposure | loser | High | Cohance explicitly flagged this margin headwind, suggesting broader sector pressure on input/logistics costs. |
| Recovery dependent on successful validation and commercialization of ADC/Oligo platforms which require long lead times. | US/EU Biotechs outsourcing complex conjugation | beneficiary | Med | NJ Bio's expanded capacity positions Cohance as a key enabler for biotechs needing scalable bioconjugation. |

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Pharma CDMO rests on '30+ year relationships with global innovators' and 'proven expertise in scaling up hazardous chemistry, complex chiral and multi step synthesis', with '20/20 Top innovator relations; contributing >85% revenues' and 18 commercial patented molecules in Small Molecules.
- API+ is framed as a 'Focused portfolio and market leadership in low-mid volume, specialty APIs with low competitive intensity', with the deck claiming 'Top 3 player in 8 out of 10 top molecules in the API portfolio'.
- In nucleic acids the deck claims Cohance is 'Amongst few CDMOs globally specialized in Oligonucleotide and mRNA building blocks including specific delivery systems and Tri-cyclo-DNA'.
- Deck states its FY26 sales mix as Pharma CDMO 39%, API+ 48%, Spec Chem 13%; for Q1 FY27 it separately states Pharma CDMO 30%, API+ 62%, Specialty Chemicals 8%, and describes 'CDMO# share at 38%' where '#CDMO includes Pharma CDMO and Speciality Chemicals'.
- Niche technology share contributed 15.1% of revenues in Q1 FY27.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Sapala stake-up] In July 2024 Cohance acquired a 67.5% stake in Sapala Organics for Rs. 258 crore; it now 'proposes to increase its ownership in Sapala', with the executive summary citing 'a defined path to full ownership of Sapala'. PPE includes assets held for sale per the Sapala SPA of Rs. 308 Mn as on Q1 FY27.
- [Sapala leadership] Founder Dr. P. Y. Reddy 'has consented to assume responsibility and lead the unlocking potential of the combined nucleic-acid business through FY29, in addition to continuing as CEO of Sapala'; customers indicated preference for 'a more end-to-end integrated nucleic-acid offering' rather than a supplier of individual building blocks. Sapala holds ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 accreditations and has a team with 'over a century of combined experience across 18 labs'.
- [Merger] The company is 'formerly, Suven Pharmaceuticals Limited'; Q1 FY26 carried an exceptional item of Rs. 81 Mn of 'one-time restructuring costs incurred due to merger of the Company with erstwhile Cohance Lifesciences Limited'.
- [NJ Bio drag] The deck attributes part of consolidated margin pressure to subsidiary consolidation from NJ Bio, which 'made EBITDA loss of Rs. 328 Mn'; NJ Bio 'Revenue has some FTE's contract risk this year' and 'profitability remains a medium-term objective'.
- [Organisation] 'All CXO positions in place'; R&D 'bolstered with large number of PhD additions'; most new hires from leading Indian pharma companies; plant heads and regional business managers onboarded.
- [Outlook] FY27 framed as a 'GROWTH YEAR, WEIGHTED TOWARDS H2' — sequential improvement expected from Q2 with growth returning during H2 FY27, supported by Pharma CDMO recovery, order-backed growth in Sapala, API+ stability and formulations normalisation.
